```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 6, message = FALSE)
library(influ2)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw())
has_glmmTMB <- requireNamespace("glmmTMB", quietly = TRUE)
```

## Two runs, one CDI display

An influence comparison asks whether two model runs tell the same story about
the effect of a covariate, its sampled distribution, and its contribution to
the annual index. `plot_cdi()` overlays the runs **within the same CDI
panels**: it does not place two complete displays beside one another.
Colours identify the model throughout. Coefficients and distribution bubbles
are slightly dodged, and influence lines share the same year axis.

This article uses the same simulated `lobsters_per_pot` observations as the
[main article](influ2.html). We fit a negative-binomial model to the full
2000--2017 series, and another to observations from 2007 onwards. We also
omit 2012 from the second run to demonstrate an internal gap. Removing a year
is only a display example, not a recommendation for model selection.

```{r comparison-lobster-models, eval=has_glmmTMB}
data(lobsters_per_pot)
full_data <- lobsters_per_pot
year_number <- as.integer(as.character(full_data$year))
recent_data <- droplevels(full_data[
  year_number >= 2007 & year_number != 2012, ])

full_model <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  lobsters ~ year + poly(depth, 3) + poly(soak, 3) + (1 | month),
  family = glmmTMB::nbinom2(), data = full_data
)
recent_model <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  lobsters ~ year + poly(depth, 3) + poly(soak, 3) + (1 | month),
  family = glmmTMB::nbinom2(), data = recent_data
)
stopifnot(full_model$fit$convergence == 0, full_model$sdr$pdHess,
  recent_model$fit$convergence == 0, recent_model$sdr$pdHess)
```

Both models have a monthly random intercept. We calculate each diagnostic
once; changing the display does not refit models or recalculate uncertainty.
Random effects are stored as one term per grouping factor, named after the
factor, so the monthly random intercept is the term `"month"`.

```{r comparison-lobster-diagnostics, eval=has_glmmTMB}
full_diagnostic <- influ(full_model, focus = "year")
recent_diagnostic <- influ(recent_model, focus = "year")
diagnostics <- list(Full = full_diagnostic, Recent = recent_diagnostic)
```

### Different year ranges and missing years

The default `years = "union"` retains the full calendar range. The recent run
has no bubbles or influence estimates before 2007 or in 2012. A missing year
is not a zero, and its influence line is not connected across the gap.
Months are matched by their labels, rather than their positions in a table.
Bubble area uses one common proportion scale for both runs.

```{r comparison-cdi-union, eval=has_glmmTMB, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Overlaid monthly coefficient-distribution-influence displays for the full 2000--2017 lobster model and a recent-period model fitted to 2007--2017 with 2012 omitted. Model colours identify two coefficient sets, dodged distribution bubbles, and influence lines within the same panels. Coefficients and influence retain each model's own reference distribution; they have not been re-centred to a common reference. Bubble area represents the within-year proportion of that model's records, using a shared size scale. Missing years remain blank, without an influence line across the internal gap.", fig.alt="One CDI display with two coloured monthly-effect estimates, two dodged bubble sets where both models have records, and two annual influence lines. The recent run starts in 2007 and has a gap in 2012."}
plot_cdi(diagnostics, term = "month", years = "union")
```

The model labels are taken from the named list. A single diagnostic is also
accepted, so `plot_cdi(full_diagnostic, term = "month")` keeps the ordinary
single-run display. The existing `plot(full_diagnostic, type = "cdi",
term = "month")` remains available.

`years = "overlap"` restricts the view to years available in every run. It is
a **display filter**, not a refit or a new calculation of the reference
distribution. The omitted 2012 still occupies its calendar position, so the
remaining years are not presented as an uninterrupted sequence.

```{r comparison-cdi-overlap, eval=has_glmmTMB, fig.height=7, fig.cap="The same stored monthly CDI results restricted to years shared by both model runs. Coefficient estimates and reference distributions are unchanged from the union display. The missing 2012 is not interpolated or treated as zero; the common year axis preserves that gap.", fig.alt="Overlaid CDI panels restricted to the common recent years, with the 2012 gap retained and the same model-specific coefficient estimates as the full-range display."}
plot_cdi(diagnostics, term = "month", years = "overlap")
```

### What is comparable?

The monthly relative effects are centred using the reference already stored
in each diagnostic. Because the runs use different observations, their
references can differ. The display makes this explicit: an apparent vertical
shift is not automatically a change in the seasonal relationship. A genuinely
shared reference must be defined when calculating the diagnostics, using
compatible reference observations and weights. Plotting compact summaries
cannot recover the joint information needed to re-centre their uncertainty.

Compare the same term, component, and effect scale. An encounter effect on the
log-odds scale is not interchangeable with a positive-component response ratio.
Categorical labels must identify the same strata in every run. Continuous
covariates need compatible evaluation grids or bin definitions: matching
rounded labels alone does not establish that compatibility.

Random-effect strata must also have verified grouping and level identifiers.
If an older diagnostic stores only an aggregate of fitted random-effect
values, recalculate it from a supported model before overlaying it. A numeric
random-effect value is not a stable stratum identifier across model runs.

## A separate index-ratio diagnostic

Overlaid index lines can conceal a substantial proportional difference,
particularly when both series decline towards zero. `index_ratio()` answers
a separate question: **how large is one annual estimate relative to a named
reference series?** `plot_index_ratio()` displays those ratios against a line
at one. It is independent of the CDI layout.

### Why ratios can help near zero

This deliberately constructed arithmetic example is **not a fitted model**:
one series is exactly twice the other in every year. Near the bottom of an
ordinary response-scale plot, the two lines look close together even though
the proportional difference has not changed. The ratio retains that
information. These values are used only to explain the display; the worked
`index_ratio()` example below uses actual calculated model indices.

```{r comparison-near-zero-values}
declining <- data.frame(Year = 2007:2017,
  Reference = exp(seq(log(0.8), log(0.0008), length.out = 11)))
declining$Alternative <- 2 * declining$Reference
declining$Ratio <- declining$Alternative / declining$Reference
stopifnot(all(declining$Ratio == 2))
```

```{r comparison-near-zero-plot, fig.height=6, fig.cap="An illustrative arithmetic example, not fitted model output. The alternative series is exactly twice the reference throughout a thousand-fold decline. Their absolute separation becomes visually small near zero in the upper panel, but the lower panel shows the unchanged ratio of two. The horizontal line at one denotes equal values, not a significance threshold.", fig.alt="Two declining illustrative series become visually close near zero, while a separate ratio panel remains at two in every year."}
declining_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(Year = declining$Year, Value = declining$Reference,
    Series = "Reference"),
  data.frame(Year = declining$Year, Value = declining$Alternative,
    Series = "Alternative")
)
overlay_example <- ggplot(declining_long, aes(Year, Value, colour = Series)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2007, 2017, by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Illustrative value", colour = NULL)
ratio_example <- ggplot(declining, aes(Year, Ratio)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(colour = "purple4") + geom_point(colour = "purple4") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2007, 2017, by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.8, 2.2)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Alternative / Reference")
patchwork::wrap_plots(overlay_example, ratio_example, ncol = 1)
```

### Compare calculated model indices

First, calculate expected-response CPUE indices for the two models. Both use
the same median depth and 24-hour soak profile, with the monthly random
effect set to zero. This is a fixed reference profile, not an average over
random months, and not an area-integrated abundance estimate. The units and
definition are therefore directly comparable without normalising the series.

```{r comparison-cpue-indices, eval=has_glmmTMB}
reference <- data.frame(depth = median(full_data$depth), soak = 24)
full_index <- cpue_index(
  full_model, year = "year", reference_data = reference,
  units = "lobsters per pot"
)
recent_index <- cpue_index(
  recent_model, year = "year", reference_data = reference,
  units = "lobsters per pot"
)
indices <- list(Full = full_index, Recent = recent_index)
```

```{r comparison-cpue-overlay, eval=has_glmmTMB, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Standardised expected lobsters per pot for the full and recent model runs, using the same depth and soak-time reference profile and monthly random effect zero. Ribbons are pointwise 95% intervals for each index separately, not uncertainty in their difference or ratio. The recent run has a shorter time range and no 2012 estimate.", fig.alt="Two standardised lobster CPUE series with individual uncertainty ribbons; the recent model covers a shorter period."}
plot_compare(indices)
```

```{r comparison-index-ratio, eval=has_glmmTMB}
recent_to_full <- index_ratio(indices, reference = "Full")
recent_to_full
```

```{r comparison-index-ratio-plot, eval=has_glmmTMB, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Annual recent-run CPUE divided by the full-run CPUE, using estimates in the same response units and the same fixed reference profile. Ratios above one mean that the recent run estimates higher CPUE. Only matching observed years can produce a ratio; years before the recent run and its omitted 2012 remain unavailable. These are point-estimate ratios, without a ratio confidence interval.", fig.alt="The recent-to-full lobster index ratio, with a horizontal reference at one and no estimates outside matching years or in 2012."}
plot_index_ratio(recent_to_full)
```

The calculation joins **year labels**, not row numbers. It does not extend a
shorter series, interpolate absent estimates, or replace zero denominators
with a small arbitrary constant. Missing or undefined ratios are reported in
the compact result rather than silently turned into observations.

The two fits share observations. Their index errors are therefore generally
dependent. Dividing the limits of two marginal confidence intervals would
not give a confidence interval for their ratio; this diagnostic deliberately
does not do so.

### Standardised versus nominal CPUE

The influence object's standardised series is a centred **year-effect
contrast**. Its nominal series is the observed annual mean response. Those
are not already in identical units. To compare their relative shapes, request
`normalise = "common"` explicitly, using the **same nominated years** for
both geometric-mean denominators. This normalisation is separate from the
reference used to calculate influence or expected-response CPUE.

```{r comparison-nominal-ratio, eval=has_glmmTMB}
standardised_to_nominal <- index_ratio(
  full_diagnostic, series = c("standardised", "nominal"),
  reference = "nominal", normalise = "common",
  baseline_years = as.character(2007:2011)
)
```

```{r comparison-nominal-ratio-plot, eval=has_glmmTMB, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="The full model's standardised year-effect contrast divided by nominal annual mean lobsters per pot, after each series is divided by its geometric mean over the same 2007--2011 baseline period. This compares relative trajectories, not absolute response units. Values above one mean that the standardised trajectory is higher relative to its common-period geometric mean than the nominal trajectory. No ratio uncertainty is implied.", fig.alt="Annual ratios of common-period-normalised standardised and nominal lobster indices, with a reference line at one."}
plot_index_ratio(standardised_to_nominal)
```

Normalising each run over its own full, different time range can manufacture
a difference in scale. If relative scaling is required for several model
runs, use `normalise = "common"` and nominate an agreed baseline available in
all of them. If absolute CPUE units are comparable and relevant to the
question, retain the default `normalise = "none"` instead.

## Reuse the calculated results

The CDI diagnostics, CPUE indices, and ratio diagnostic are calculated
objects. Reprinting them or changing plot labels, colours, or layout does
not fit another model, run MCMC, or regenerate an observation-by-simulation
matrix. See [CPUE indices](cpue-indices.html) for annual tables, joint
covariance, and area integration, and [Model search](model-search.html) for
constrained searches whose selected native fit can feed these interfaces.
